module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# A108306: Expansion of $(3x+1)/(1-3x-3x^2)$

This sequence satisfies the linear recurrence relation $a(0)=1$, $a(1)=6$,
and $a(n) = 3a(n-1) + 3a(n-2)$ for $n \ge 2$.

*References:*
- [A108306](https://oeis.org/A108306)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA108306

/-- The primary defining sequence `a`.
`a n` is the $n$-th term of the expansion of $(3x+1)/(1-3x-3x^2)$,
satisfying $a(0)=1, a(1)=6, a(n)=3a(n-1)+3a(n-2)$. -/
def a : ℕ → ℕ
  | 0 => 1
  | 1 => 6
  | k + 2 => 3 * a (k + 1) + 3 * a k

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_0 : a 0 = 1 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_1 : a 1 = 6 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_2 : a 2 = 21 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_3 : a 3 = 81 := by decide

@[category test, AMS 11]
theorem a_4 : a 4 = 306 := by decide

open Matrix

/--
The matrix for the specific case $a=5, b=2$.
$$M = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 5 \cr 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$$
-/
def m : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℕ :=
  fun i j => match i, j with
  | 0, 0 => 1
  | 0, 1 => 5
  | 1, 0 => 1
  | 1, 1 => 2

/--
The sequence is the INVERT transform of (1, 5, 10, 20, 40, 80, 160, ...) and can be obtained
by extracting the upper left terms of matrix powers of [(1,5); (1,2)].
These results are a case (a=5, b=2) of the general conjecture below.
-/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem a_is_invert_transform_case (n : ℕ) :
    a n = (m ^ (n + 1)) 0 0 := by
  -- `m` satisfies `m ^ 2 = 3 m + 3`, so its powers satisfy the recurrence of `a`.
  have hm : ∀ n, m ^ (n + 2) = 3 • m ^ (n + 1) + 3 • m ^ n := fun n => by
    rw [pow_add, show m ^ 2 = 3 • m + 3 • (1 : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℕ) by decide, mul_add,
      mul_smul_comm, mul_smul_comm, mul_one, ← pow_succ]
  induction n using Nat.twoStepInduction with
  | zero => decide
  | one => decide
  | more k ih1 ih2 =>
    rw [a, ih1, ih2, show k + 2 + 1 = k + 1 + 2 by omega, hm (k + 1)]
    simp only [Matrix.add_apply, Matrix.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]

/--
The c sequence for the general INVERT transform conjecture.
$c(1) = 1$, $c(k)=ab^(k-2)$ for $k \ge 2$.
-/
def invertSeqC (a b : ℕ) : ℕ → ℕ
  | 0 => 0
  | 1 => 1
  | (k + 2) => a * b^k

/-- The INVERT transform of the sequence c. -/
noncomputable def invertSeqD (a b : ℕ) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Nat.strongRecOn n
    (fun m ih =>
      if m = 0 then 1
      else ∑ i ∈ Finset.range m,
        if h : i < m then invertSeqC a b (m - i) * ih i h else 0)

/-- The general 2x2 matrix [(1,a); (1,b)]. -/
def genMatrix (a b : ℕ) : Matrix (Fin 2) (Fin 2) ℕ :=
  fun i j => match i, j with
  | 0, 0 => 1
  | 0, 1 => a
  | 1, 0 => 1
  | 1, 1 => b

/--
The conjecture: The INVERT transform of a sequence starting
$(1, a, ab, ab^2, ab^3, \ldots)$ is equivalent to extracting the upper left terms
of powers of the 2x2 matrix [(1,a); (1,b)].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at
    "https://github.com/KitaKen1/oeis-108306/blob/2e01e81b20a56880993e174ee4af0f0d7af37bdd/lean/OeisA108306FC.lean#L101-L106"]
theorem conjecture (a_val b_val n : ℕ) :
    invertSeqD a_val b_val n = (genMatrix a_val b_val ^ n) 0 0 := by
  sorry

end OeisA108306

reformulations.difference: The helpers use one-based input indexing with invertSeqC a b 0 = 0 and prepend invertSeqD a b 0 = 1 to the transformed sequence. The theorem consequently includes the zeroth matrix power. For a=5, b=2, invertSeqD begins 1,1,6,21,..., whereas OEIS displays 1,6,21,..., obtained from positive matrix powers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The standard INVERT definition is 1 + Σ_{n≥1} t_n x^n = 1/(1 − Σ_{n≥1} c_n x^n). Its coefficient recurrence is precisely invertSeqD's recurrence with d_0=1. Thus, when T denotes the zero-indexed displayed transform, T(n)=invertSeqD a b (n+1). In /workspace/review/Checks.lean, I independently defined this zero-indexed transform by its convolution recurrence, proved sourceInv_eq, and proved full_indexing_iff: the file's universally quantified identity is equivalent to T(n)=(genMatrix a b ^ (n+1)) 0 0. The extra n=0 case is simply 1=1.

sources_consulted: OEIS A108306, including Gary W. Adamson's July 31, 2016 conjecture and N.-E. Fahssi's recurrence: https://oeis.org/A108306. Full entry read via the official OEIS data mirror at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oeis/oeisdata/main/seq/A108/A108306.seq because direct OEIS requests were blocked.

Mira Bernstein and N. J. A. Sloane, Some Canonical Sequences of Integers, Section 1, INVERT definition: https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0205301; LaTeX source read from https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0205301.

review.notes: Checked all 12 declarations. The defining recurrence and five initial-value tests match OEIS, and the special-case matrix identity is faithful. Unfolding strong recursion confirms the INVERT convolution; membership in Finset.range n ensures n−i≥1, so truncated subtraction and the artificial c(0) cannot change it. An executable recurrence, proved equal to invertSeqD, passed all 396 matrix comparisons with 0≤a,b≤5 and 0≤n≤10. The cited external proof compiled against this checkout and its theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, supporting both research solved and formal_proof metadata. The file's completed proofs were also checked for axioms. Scratch checks and the indexing equivalence are in /workspace/review/Checks.lean. No repository files were edited.
